title: Keys and required properties
summary: Choosing primary keys (generated, natural, composite, Guid) and saying what must have a value.

steps.title: Every entity needs a key
body: The **primary key** identifies a row. EF Core uses it for everything: finding a row with `Find`, knowing which row an `UPDATE` targets, linking rows together.
You have used the convention (`Id` or `BookId`). When the key has another name, say so with `[Key]`:
[Key] public string Code { get; set; } = "";    // "KE", "UG": a natural key
| `Guid` | `Guid Id` | EF Core, before the insert |
| natural | `string Code` | you: you must set it |

A natural key is something the real world already uses. It reads well, but if it can ever change (an email address, a phone number), prefer a generated key and put a **unique index** on the natural value instead (lesson 4).

steps.prompt: A `User` entity is keyed by `Email`. A user changes their email address. What is the problem?
options: The primary key changes, and every row that refers to the user by that key must change too
SQLite cannot store strings as keys
EF Core will generate a new email automatically
steps.explain: Keys are what other rows point at. A key that changes ripples through every reference. EF Core does not even allow changing the key of a tracked entity: you would have to delete and re-insert.

steps.title: Composite keys
body: Some rows are identified by a **combination** of values. An enrolment is "this student in this course": the pair is unique, neither half is.
Since EF Core 7 you can say that with an attribute on the class:
The table gets `CONSTRAINT "PK_Enrollments" PRIMARY KEY ("StudentId", "CourseId")`, and `Find` takes both values in key order: `db.Enrollments.Find(7, 2)`.
Composite keys are never generated: you set both parts.

code: protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=school.db");
steps.explain: `Find` takes the key values in the order the key declares them: student first, then course. `Find(20, 1)` asks for student 20 in course 1, which does not exist.

steps.title: Required and optional
body: Whether a column accepts `NULL` comes from the C# type, as you saw: `string` is required, `string?` optional.
- **`[Required]`** makes a column `NOT NULL` even when the C# type is nullable. Useful in older code without nullable reference types.

- **`[MaxLength(100)]`** records the maximum length. SQL Server turns it into `nvarchar(100)` and rejects longer values. **SQLite ignores lengths** (its `TEXT` has no limit), so the rule is not enforced there.
[Required] public string? Email { get; set; }     // NOT NULL despite the ?
public string? Phone { get; set; }               // NULL allowed

> **Tip:** Database rules are your last line of defence, not your validation. Check input where it arrives (an API endpoint) and give a friendly error; let the database guarantee the rule holds no matter what.

steps.prompt: Will SQLite store the row, or refuse it?
items: `Phone = null` when the property is `string? Phone`
`Email = null` when it is `[Required] string? Email`
Two rows with the same primary key
steps.explain: `NOT NULL` and primary keys are enforced by SQLite. Maximum lengths are recorded in the model but SQLite does not check them; SQL Server would refuse that row.

code: protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=shop.db");
steps.explain: A `Guid` key is generated by EF Core itself, as soon as the entity is added, not by the database on insert. So the id is known before `SaveChanges`, which is handy when you need it right away (to build a URL, say). Each one is different.

steps.prompt: Complete the entity: `Isbn` is the key, `Title` is required with a maximum length of 200, and `Subtitle` is optional.
steps.explain: `[Key]` names a key that is not called `Id`. A non-nullable `string` is already required, so only the length needs saying. `string?` makes the column optional.

steps.title: A country table
prompt: Write a `Country` entity and an `AtlasDb` context (`Data Source=atlas.db`, a `DbSet<Country>` named `Countries`).
- `Code` (string) is the primary key, for example `"KE"`.
The tests check the generated schema and that `Find("UG")` works.
solution: protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=atlas.db");
template: Dojo.Check("Code is the primary key", dojoSql.Contains("\"Code\" TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT \"PK_Countries\" PRIMARY KEY"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Capital is optional", dojoSql.Contains("\"Capital\" TEXT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Population is required", dojoSql.Contains("\"Population\" INTEGER NOT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Eq("Name has a maximum length of 60", 60, dojoDb.Model.FindEntityType(typeof(Country))?.FindProperty("Name")?.GetMaxLength());
dojoDb.Countries.Add(new Country { Code = "UG", Name = "Uganda", Capital = "Kampala", Population = 45_000_000 });
